mistakes.note: Opening narration sets the scene at about eight in the morning, but the record says early afternoon and the next replies call it grey afternoon with no time passing.

Grout, the killer and the smugglers' muscle, explains to the nosy widow on first asking that the tallies count kegs and landings, who the half-names are, that Crane kept the count six years and that Crane and the reverend had words Sunday.
Grout owns the button from the drowning spot out loud ('That's mine, then') to the woman investigating him.
Plot Thread now and Kit's record say Harriet's girl had Kit in the loft before dark and Grout found the shed empty, while M50 and M54 have Kit still in the shed and Grout finding him there.
PC status stays 'unhurt' with a wrenched wrist after the page and Known facts say Grout broke it.
Thorne says Grout sent word 'an hour since' about the lane, though the lane scene happened minutes before and Nell hurried straight up.
Thorne repeats Grout's threat that 'the vicar would hear of it', which only Nell heard and which she had not told him; the page never marks it as a slip.
Thorne goes from vowing to keep her locked in the dark until she gives her word to unlocking the door and escorting her about town, for nothing in return.
Plot Thread now puts Grout waiting in the dark by the stable stair while the page has him drinking at the counter.
Harriet speaks of the bad-heart story that Thorne put only to Nell in the locked study; no telling is shown.
Harriet knows the half-names belong to the county men, which only Grout told Nell.
Harriet guesses sixty pages and the book runs thirty-odd from March to October, while Grout said Crane kept the count six years without a slip.
Owen Price's record says he knows Mrs Ashby laid out the body, hours before she did.
Looks keep passing states: Thorne's hat on, off, on the desk; Kit's boots and cap; Grout 'sweating'; Thorne's and Kit's portraits are redrawn for them.
A Loose End says Price means to come to Nell at first light, which is the hidden Plot Thread plan, never learned on the page.
Loose Ends go stale and stay open: Kit won't enter the crypt while Grout digs, Thorne 'stood over me with his hat... I have not yet told him what Grout did', the spare room for tonight.
Journal says Harriet has the ledger in her apron pocket when the page put the folded oilcloth there; Known NPCs calls Harriet 'a widow like me', invented; facts are added twice at rounds 35 and 37.
A Choice offers to bind the wrist with the shawl, already done at M60.
The laying-out scene shows no body on the slab, only a large sheet of paper she seems to read.
Drawn outside on the open quay rather than inside the boat-shed, and Kit's smock is painted as a grey skirt (again at M94).
The woman behind the Anchor's bar is a young stranger, not Harriet.
A fire burns in the hearth that the narration says was laid and unlit.
Grout is in a brown coat instead of his black wool one.

choices.reason: Three distinct, in-voice paths nearly every round and picks bend what follows (the gate trick, the night trip to the cottage); one stale Choice.

surprise.reason: The world acts on its own: Grout takes the button, catches Kit, breaks the wrist, Thorne locks the study; but much of the truth arrives by Grout explaining it.

threads.reason: Grout's and Harriet's threads move well within the evening, but Price never reaches the page and the hidden nows drift from the page twice.

characters.reason: Strong voices, but Grout spills the smuggling and owns the button, Thorne turns from jailer to escort without cause, and Harriet knows things she was never told.

continuity.reason: Small slips a careful reader catches: morning vs afternoon at the start, Grout's word 'an hour since', ledger length; none breaks a scene.

pacing.reason: Every reply adds a fact or a turn; the locked-study standoff runs a few rounds but each one escalates.

prose.reason: Vivid, period-true voice with concrete detail; a few repeated gestures (hats, palms flat) but few tics.

pictures.reason: Faces and clothes mostly right and wrist binding tracked, but a laying-out with no body, a wrong Harriet, Kit in a skirt, a lit fire and the wrong coat.

secrets.reason: Body clues and the ledger are found on the page, but Grout hands over the smuggling truth on first asking and a Loose End leaks Price's hidden plan.

agency.reason: Moves are carried out as given; the PC speaks and decides only within them.

stakes.reason: Risky moves are checked and failures cost real things carried forward (button lost, broken wrist, locked in), though Checks also land on trivial moves.

state.reason: A string of mostly hidden faults: thread nows against the page, 'unhurt' with a broken wrist, passing states in looks with redrawn portraits, stale Loose Ends, wrong Journal entries.

mystery.reason: Fair physical clues are planted and found (button, black wool, fingertip bruises, receipt, tallies), but the crypt's meaning comes from the sexton explaining it and the ledger's hiding place from Crane's note, so the truth is handed over more than deduced.
